lenses.summary:
Motion-craft audit (read-only: code, curl of the live site, screenshots). Tifo already owns a great motif, the tifo card, a fan's card turning over. Right now it is diluted. The goal moment is a generic full-screen colour wash that hides the stand. The score "flip" wobbles digits that have already changed. The key art shows up last, after the rest of the hero has assembled piece by piece. On top of that, several infinite animations break DESIGN-v3's own rule that motion only answers something.

Fix four live bugs first, tonight's match included:
1. A false «هدف» fires on page load because the prerendered HTML is up to about 30 minutes stale.
2. The crest view-transition names are wiped by the first data poll.
3. The skeleton shimmer hides real empty messages.
4. The goal whistle is usually silent.

Then make three moves iconic, all built from the one card motif:
- **Card-stunt goal.** The stand flips to the scorer's colours and spells the new score.
- **Split-flap digits.** Only the changed digit flips, and live cards and rows get a short "just scored" state.
- **Instant stand at first paint.** The card-raise intro plays once per session.

These follow patterns people already know: real card stunts in the stands, stadium split-flap boards, Apple Sports' rolling numbers, and Paris-2024-style consistency of one motif.

The remaining findings are phone and battery hygiene:
- Three backdrop blurs behind panels that are more than 92% opaque.
- An always-on breathing scrim and a paint-bound live dot.
- 20-second polls that rewrite seven sections even when nothing changed.
- A 3D pitch with about 540 separate meshes.
- Stacked sticky bars with two share icons.
- Sheets that the Android back gesture doesn't close.

Items 387–403 are not re-proposed. 400 (per-digit `.cell`) and 401 (floodlights) are used as foundations. One gap is flagged: the feed has no period_start or clock, so a live-ticking minute isn't possible yet. Key files: /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/shell.js, src/keyart.js, src/app.js, src/v3.css, src/tifo.css, src/pitch3d.js, build.cjs.

findings.title: False «هدف» flash (and whistle) on opening a live match page
findings.evidence: site/src/shell.js:180 seeds lastScore from the prerendered #msum. The HTML is stale during live play: at 17:53 UTC, /m/6052084/ had last-modified 17:25 with minute 60, while /v1/live.json (17:52) showed 0-1 at 95'. The first poll (app.js:351-353 run(), then 147 tifo:match, then shell.js:151 scoreWatch) sees a score increase and fires the full-screen goalfx for a goal scored up to about 30 minutes earlier. This happens every time a goal lands between two builds, tonight included.
findings.proposal: Never fire goalMoment on the first tifo:match or tifo:day of a page view. Seed lastScore from the first fetched JSON instead of #msum, for example by setting a `seeded` flag in scoreWatch and returning early on the first call. Apply the same guard to the home hero handler at shell.js:182.
findings.verified:
Code, ~/workspace/saas/football/site/src/shell.js lines 163-183. goalMoment() adds a full-screen .goalfx «هدف» overlay and calls whistle(). scoreWatch() fires it whenever md.score is higher than lastScore[id]. On match pages, lastScore is seeded from the prerendered #msum (line 181), and a missing score is seeded as {0,0}. app.js match() runs from run() on load and dispatches tifo:match with fresh /v1/match JSON on the first fetch, so any gap between the prerender and the live data fires the goal moment on page open. Nothing in the code guards against this.

Live check at 18:23 UTC: /m/6052085/ (Bahrain v UAE) had last-modified 17:55 and its #msum said status "scheduled" with score null. /v1/match/6052085.json said live, 0-0, minute 23. No false flash yet because it is still 0-0, but the first goal will make every page open fire «هدف» until the page is rebuilt. /m/6052084/ still had #msum live 0-1 at 84' while the JSON said finished 0-1, which shows the HTML runs behind the JSON. The auditor's 17:53 snapshot fits this.

Two parts of the claim are wrong. (1) The whistle is off by default: whistle() returns unless localStorage tifo.goalsnd is "1". (2) The home hero is not affected: lastScore is seeded only when PAGE==="match", so on home the first tifo:day finds p undefined, only seeds the score, and does not fire.
findings.corrected: Confirmed on match pages only. shell.js:181 seeds lastScore from the prerendered #msum, and a missing score becomes {0,0}. The #msum runs behind the live JSON: tonight /m/6052085/ was built at 17:55 as "scheduled" with no score while the match was live at 23'. So the first tifo:match after load fires the full-screen «هدف» overlay (goalMoment at shell.js:163) for any goal scored after the last build. The whistle plays only for users who turned on the goal sound, which is off by default. The home hero handler (shell.js:183) does not have this bug, because lastScore is empty on home and the first tifo:day only seeds it. Fix: in scoreWatch, seed from the first fetched JSON and return without firing. For example, drop the #msum seeding of lastScore at line 181 and keep heroState(m0), so the first call finds p undefined and only seeds. No change is needed for the home handler.

findings.title: Crest view transitions (356) are wiped by the first poll
findings.evidence: shell.js:129 sets img.style.viewTransitionName once. Then app.js:147 set('#mh') and the home stand() set('#standcap') replace those nodes after the load fetch (run() at app.js:353), so the names are gone within about 1s and the morph essentially never happens. The hero crests are also loading="lazy" (curl of / and /m/6052085/).
findings.proposal:
1. Emit style="view-transition-name:crest-ID" inside R.matchHead, R.heroLine and the team hero markup, so both the build and every re-render carry it.
2. On click of an a.rc or day row, name only that card's two crests and its .dg (score-ID) just before navigating. The same match sits in r-live, r-today and #day, so naming all of them would duplicate names and abort the transition.
3. Give .top and .tabbar their own view-transition-name so the chrome stays still instead of cross-fading.
4. Make hero crests loading=eager with fetchpriority=high.
findings.verified: Checked the source and the live bundle. src/shell.js:129 is deployed as /assets/shell.6b99163974.js and sets img.style.viewTransitionName="crest-ID" once, on .hero img.logo. On the live pages, script order is app.js and then shell.js. On the home page (curl of /), the hero crests 5892 and 5902 sit inside div#standcap. stand() at app.js:79 runs set("#standcap", R.standCap(m)), and set() at app.js:15 swaps innerHTML, so it replaces those img nodes after the home() fetch and on every poll (20s while live). On /m/6052085/, the crests 5901 and 5789 sit inside #mh, and match() at app.js:148 replaces them with set("#mh", R.matchHead(md)) on load and on every poll. So the name is gone from both pages that send a crest to the team page soon after load. The team hero on /t/5789/ (.thero, one logo xl 5789) is never re-rendered: team() at app.js:156 only sets #next and #past, so it keeps its name. Every hero crest on /, /m/ and /t/ is served with loading="lazy". I found nothing that re-applies the name after a re-render. v3.css:433 turns on cross-document view transitions with @view-transition{navigation:auto}.
findings.corrected: Mostly true. The claim is right that home and match wipe the names. It is wrong about the team page. There, team() only rewrites #next and #past, and the hero crest keeps its name. So "the morph essentially never happens" is too strong. Home or match to the team page is broken once the load fetch has returned, because the outgoing page has lost the name. Team page to match or home probably still morphs, but this is inferred and was not tested in a browser. The reason is that the incoming page takes its snapshot after shell.js has run and before the fetch resolves. The fix is still valid. Put view-transition-name inside R.matchHead and R.standCap/heroLine so every re-render carries it. When a list card is clicked, name that card's crests just before navigating, and never give two elements the same name. Make hero crests eager with fetchpriority=high.

findings.title: Skeleton CSS hides real empty/error messages forever
findings.evidence:
v3.css:430 applies `#tv > .empty, #pout > .empty, #kitct > .empty, #lplot > .empty {color:transparent; animation:skel infinite}`. The final states use the same class: app.js:196 renders `

ما في مباريات اليوم.

` into #tv, and lab.js:12 renders «ما في أرقام كافية.». On a day with no matches, شاشة المجلس is an endless shimmer with an invisible message.
findings.proposal: Give the build's loading placeholders (build.cjs:531 and :525 «نحمّل…/نجهّز…») a separate class `.skel`, and point the shimmer at `.skel` only, capped at 3 iterations. `.empty` stays readable.
findings.verified:
The rule the auditor describes is live. src/v3.css:430 matches the shipped /assets/tifo.6b99163974.css: `#tv > .empty,#pout > .empty,#kitct > .empty,#lplot > .empty,#cout:empty{block-size:10rem;color:transparent;...;animation:skel 1.4s linear infinite}`. The final messages use the same `.empty` class. In src/app.js:189-196, tv() writes `

ما في مباريات اليوم.

` into #tv when there are no matches. This includes the case where the day and live fetches fail, because those errors are caught and turned into an empty match list. After that it calls poll(tv, 20e3), so /tv/ shows a shimmer with no visible text for the whole day. In src/lab.js:12, «ما في أرقام كافية.» goes into #lplot (box = $("#lplot")), and that message is hidden the same way. The loading placeholders are the ones the auditor names: build.cjs:531 («نحمّل المباريات…»), :525 («نجهّز الجدول…»), :312 («نحمّل الأرقام…») and :610 (#lplot «نحمّل…»). The reduced-motion rule (v3.css:431) only stops the animation. The text stays transparent. Two parts of the claim do not hold. #pout has no final `.empty` state: compare.js writes no `.empty`. #kitct has none either: app.js:265-267 only writes the table. So only #tv and #lplot are affected.
findings.corrected: The claim is right for #tv (شاشة المجلس on a day with no matches, which keeps shimmering because it re-polls every 20 seconds) and for #lplot (lab «ما في أرقام كافية.»). It is wrong for #pout and #kitct, which never render a final `.empty` message. The proposal works: put `.skel` on the 4 build placeholders (build.cjs:312, 525, 531, 610) and point the v3.css:430-431 selectors at `.skel` instead of `.empty`. For #cout, keep the `:empty` rule. Leave the reduced-motion override in place. `color:transparent` should also apply only to `.skel`.

findings.title: Goal whistle is usually silent (AudioContext never resumed)
findings.evidence: shell.js:137 whistle() creates the AudioContext lazily at goal time and there is no resume() anywhere in shell.js. Chrome and Safari start a context in the suspended state if it is created without prior user activation. A phone left on the table since load stays mute even with the setting on.
findings.proposal: When tifo.goalsnd is '1', create the AudioContext and call AC.resume() on the first pointerdown or keydown anywhere (once). If it is still suspended at goal time, show a small «اضغط عشان يشتغل الصوت» chip in the mini-bar. navigator.vibrate needs the same armed gesture (see the goal-moment finding).
findings.verified: I read ~/workspace/saas/football/site/src/shell.js lines 154-168 and fetched the live bundle https://tifo.elyoxe.com/assets/shell.6b99163974.js, which has the same code. whistle() is at line 157, not 137. It does `AC = AC || new AudioContext()` and never calls resume(). There is no resume() and no other AudioContext anywhere in src/ or redesign/src/. goalMoment() (line 168) calls whistle() from a score poll, which is never a user gesture. The only time the context gets made during a gesture is the #goalsnd toggle's onclick (line 155), which runs whistle() when the sound is switched on. The claim's core holds, with two corrections below.
findings.corrected: [broken/medium] The goal whistle is often silent after a page load. It is at shell.js:157, not 137. The sound works in the page session where the user switches it on, because the #goalsnd onclick creates the AudioContext during that tap. On every later page load the setting is still stored, but the context is only created at goal time, from a poll with no gesture, and no resume() is ever called. On iOS Safari the context stays suspended unless it is created or resumed inside a gesture, so the whistle is effectively always mute there. On Chrome for Android it only plays if the user has already tapped the page (sticky activation), so a phone left on the table since load stays silent. Proposal: when tifo.goalsnd is '1', create the context and call AC.resume() once, on the first pointerdown or keydown. At goal time, call AC.resume() before scheduling the sound, and if the state is still 'suspended', show the «اضغط عشان يشتغل الصوت» chip.

findings.title: Signature 1: turn the goal moment into a real card stunt, scoped to the hero
findings.evidence: feat_goal.png: the 55% full-viewport wash (v3.css:390) tints the whole UI, tab bar included, like a disabled modal. The name sweeps from -60vw to 60vw, left to right (v3.css:392-394), so it never holds still, and it moves against the RTL reading direction. The stand wave that keyart.set() already sends from the scorer's side, which is the actual signature, sits under the wash. On home it fires for the hero match even when the user is 2000px down.
findings.proposal:
Drop the full-screen wash.
1. The stand's cards flip column by column from the scorer's side into the scorer's colours and spell the new score. To build the mask, fillText the score in Barlow into an offscreen cols×rows canvas and read it with getImageData; mask cells turn chalk. Hold 2s, then flip back.
2. «هدف» and the scorer's name slide in from the scorer's side and hold 1.5s on the hero's night floor.
3. If the hero is off-screen, the mini-bar takes the moment: a 1.2s club-stripe fill plus the digit flap.
4. On home, show it only if the hero is in view; otherwise pulse that rail card.
5. My-team goal: dune underline plus vibrate([40,60,40]) once the gesture is armed. A goal against my team gets only a quiet flap.
6. Score goes down (VAR): reverse flap plus the line «ألغي الهدف».
Keep prefers-reduced-motion support.

findings.title: Signature 2: true split-flap digits and a 'just scored' state on cards and rows
findings.area: score digits everywhere (hero, mini, rail, day list)
findings.evidence: v3.css:395 flip3 rotates the .dg that app.js:147 has already re-rendered (the tifo:match dispatch comes after set('#mh')), so it wobbles new to new, and the whole '1 - 0' string flips. Rail cards and day rows are silently replaced on each poll (shell.js tifo:day innerHTML), so a goal in a non-hero match gets no reaction at all.
findings.proposal: Build on item 400's per-digit .cell. Keep the previous value; for each changed cell only, fold the old top half down (180ms, clip-path halves on ::before/::after) to reveal the new bottom half (180ms), the way a stadium board or Apple Sports' numeric roll works. Use the same component in .rc .dg, day rows and the mini-bar. When a card or row's score rises, add .just for 60s: the top edge flashes the scorer's club colour once, and a small «هدف» tag sits beside the minute. No loops.

findings.title: Signature 3: the stand should be there at first paint; the intro plays once per session
findings.evidence: On home the canvas is mounted only after the index, day and live fetches resolve (app.js stand() from home()), then requestIdleCallback (600ms) plus a 1.1s wipe (keyart.js intro/blit). On other pages shell.js:72 waits for idle (700ms) and the intro waits for idle again. Result: up to about 1.3s of empty night hero, then the art wipes in. Meanwhile the lazy crests pop in and the stale live score snaps (home HTML at 17:23 showed 0-0 61' while live was 0-1 95'). The hero assembles in stages instead of arriving as one entrance, and the wipe does not read as cards.
findings.proposal:
1. build.cjs emits the static mosaic as a tiny per-page PNG, one pixel per card, scaled with image-rendering:pixelated under a 2px night grid (repeating-linear-gradient). No JS, visible at first paint; the canvas takes over only for motion.
2. The intro becomes a card raise: per frame about 33 drawImage column strips with scaleY, right to left, as cheap as the wipe. It plays on the first page of a session only (sessionStorage flag) and is static afterwards.
3. Prerendered live digits render dimmed (data-stale) until the first poll, then flap to the fresh value.

findings.title: Scrolled match page stacks 3 top bars with 2 share icons
findings.evidence: next_live_390_scrolled_final.png: top bar (share at y≈28), plus mini-bar with a second share icon (y≈79), plus sticky tabs. That is about 155px of top chrome, plus a 60px bottom bar, roughly 26% of an 844px screen. Styles at v3.css:98 and :109 (mini-on .mtabs top = topH+3rem).
findings.proposal: When .mini-on is set, slide .top up (translateY(-100%), 220ms) and dock the mini-bar at top:0. Its crests act as the brand; remove its share button. Tabs stick at 3rem. Show the top bar again on scroll-up (hide-on-scroll-down, as FotMob and Apple Sports do). This saves about 56px of reading space on every scrolled match view.

findings.title: Sheets and panel ignore the Android back gesture, can't be dragged, and vanish with no exit motion
findings.evidence: shell.js open() only toggles hidden; the panel uses history.replaceState (shell.js ~l.38). On Android, Back leaves the page instead of closing the sheet. There are no touch handlers (grep finds no touchstart or pointermove in shell.js except the desktop logo tilt). closeAll sets hidden instantly, while opening animates (sheetIn at v3.css:218).
findings.proposal:
1. pushState({sheet}) on open; popstate closes the sheet.
2. Add a 40px grab handle: translateY follows the finger (pointer events, transform only), and a pull past 80px or a fast flick closes the sheet.
3. Add a 180ms exit animation (reverse sheetIn), then set hidden.
This is native bottom-sheet behaviour, the thing phone users notice first.

findings.title: Always-on animation and blur keep the GPU busy for the whole match (battery)
findings.evidence:
DESIGN-v3 §3.9 says only the key art animates, and only in answer to something. In the code:
- `body[data-state=live] .mhero .scrim {animation:livepulse infinite}` (v3.css:401) runs for about 2h.
- `.cardflip` keyframes animate background (tifo.css:26-27), which forces a main-thread paint every frame per live dot: 6 on home now (curl /), 20+ on a busy day.
- backdrop-filter:blur(10px) sits on .top.solid (#…eb, about 92% opaque) at v3.css:23, .tabbar (f2) at :39 and .mini (f2) at :98. The blur is invisible at that opacity but is re-computed on every scroll frame.
findings.proposal:
1. Make cardflip transform-only: two faces, with the colour swap done by opacity. It runs 2 cycles, re-triggered when a poll changes the minute (a heartbeat on update).
2. Delete livepulse, or play one breath per data update.
3. Remove backdrop-filter below 880px and use solid #0A2620 or #061B16.

findings.title: Touch wave and JS parallax fight on the main thread during scroll
findings.evidence: keyart.js:15 fires a wave on every pointerdown on the canvas. The home hero is 86svh (v3.css:50), so most scroll gestures start there, and each redraws about 2,000 cells per frame for 2.6s. Meanwhile shell.js:81 does parallax by writing style.transform from a scroll-handler rAF on the main thread, so the parallax and fade stutter exactly while scrolling on mid-range Android.
findings.proposal:
1. Fire the wave on `click` (a tap without movement) instead of pointerdown.
2. Move the parallax and title fade to CSS scroll-driven animation (`animation-timeline: scroll(root)` on the canvas and .hero-in, inside @supports), which runs on the compositor in Chrome 115+ and Safari 26. Other browsers get a static hero.
3. Delete the JS scroll transform.

findings.title: 20-second polls rewrite 7 match sections (and the whole day list) even when nothing changed
findings.evidence: app.js:147 calls set() on #mh, #facts, #catchup, #events, #lineups, #stats and #h2h via innerHTML on every live poll, and app.js:68 rewrites the whole #day list. Crests are re-created, VT names are lost, and a new event just appears. Scrolling at poll time gets a long frame. shell.js already avoids this for rails (`if (box.innerHTML !== x[1])`).
findings.proposal: Skip everything when md.generated has not changed. Otherwise keep a lastHTML string per section and write only the sections that differ. When #events grows, give the new li a .new class that slides it 8px in from its team's side (220ms). No other motion.

findings.title: 3D pitch is heavy for mid-range phones (about 700 draw calls, constant autoRotate)
findings.evidence: pitch3d.js:54-56 builds 2 stands of 6×45 separate Meshes (540). Each of the 22 player cards is a 6-material box. The renderer uses antialias:true at DPR up to 2 (l.46) with MeshStandardMaterial, and the rAF loop plus autoRotate re-render every frame while the pitch is in view (l.71, l.85). The phone runs hot.
findings.proposal:
1. Use 2 InstancedMesh per stand (4 draw calls in total).
2. Cap DPR at 1.5 and turn antialias off when DPR ≥ 2.
3. Use MeshLambert.
4. Stop autoRotate after one orbit, then render only on the controls' 'change' event.
5. Hide the button when navigator.deviceMemory ≤ 3.
If even that feels gratuitous for a simple site, remove the feature.

findings.title: Cinema mode is plain and leaves the screen awake after closing
findings.evidence: feat_cinema.png: a flat radial gradient, a small score floating mid-screen, and a lot of empty space. In shell.js:168-170, navigator.wakeLock.request() is called but the sentinel is never kept or released when .x closes, so the screen stays on until the tab hides.
findings.proposal:
1. Keep the sentinel and release it on close.
2. Use the stand mosaic of both clubs full-bleed at 40% behind giant .cell digits, which also makes cinema the stage for the card-stunt goal.
3. In landscape, lay out as crest | score | crest across the full width, with the last event in one line under it.

findings.title: A live-ticking minute needs period_start/clock in the feed
findings.evidence: curl /v1/live.json returns period_start:null and clock:null, with minute as a string (e.g. '95'). The minute only changes on each 20s poll (plus the 10s CDN max-age), and it cannot tick honestly on the client.
findings.proposal: Add period_start (UTC) to live.json and match JSON in the ingest. The hero and mini-bar can then tick the minute locally, with a 1px seconds hairline under it (transform scaleX, compositor). Until then, don't fake it.

lenses.summary:
Tifo's IA has one core problem: visitor country barely changes the site. Country only sets the time zone and re-sorts the day list. The hero, the countdown (hardcoded to team 5789), المزيد «اختصارات», the competitions grid and /competitions/, /week/ and search all stay UAE-first. That contradicts the owner's «لكل العرب» decision.

Tap counts (390px phone):
- **Club to its own table:** 3+ taps plus a scroll. Club pages have no link to their league at all.
- **Home to a national team's fixtures:** 3 taps (المنتخبات → row → «المباريات والنتايج»).
- **A Moroccan or Premier League fan to their league:** 1 tap plus about 1600px or 5300px of scrolling.
- **«فريقك» on home:** slot 5, at about y 1470 of 3437.

Confirmed breakages:
- **Android back:** it leaves the page instead of closing a sheet, the reader panel or search. There is no pushState or popstate handling.
- **Tab bar:** it doesn't highlight /national/*, /week/, /arabs/, clubs or players.
- **/today/:** it never polls, so it showed «اليمن 61' 0-0 مباشر» while the live feed had 0-1.
- **Mismatched link:** the «مباريات العرب» rail header links to «مباريات بكرة».
- **Duplicate pages:** the UAE national team has 3 URLs (/uae/, /t/5789/, /national/ae/).
- **Orphaned hubs:** /arabs/ and about 16 pan-Arab pages, including the per-country TV /guide/, are missing from the nav, المزيد and the footer.

Overload:
- **المزيد:** 26 items over 2 screens.
- **League الأرقام tab:** 28 tiles.
- **Match tabs:** they overflow at 390px.
- **Hidden features:** cinema mode and the lineup maker sit behind the share icon.

Two proposals need the owner, because they change DESIGN-v3 rules:
- **Nav:** swap «الأسبوع», a static UAE-first list of 12 matches, for «فريقي». Every major competitor has Following in the bottom bar.
- **Home:** drop the «اليوم» and «مباريات العرب» rails, which repeat the list, and move «فريقك» up under the hero.

Nothing here repeats items 387–403, 345, 351 or 353.

findings.title: Android back gesture leaves the page instead of closing the sheet, panel or search
findings.evidence:
- **No history handling:** open() and closeAll() (shell.js:14-17) never call pushState, and there is no popstate handler anywhere in src/*.js.
- **What happens:** open a «من تيفو» tile, المزيد or the share sheet and swipe back. You leave the page and lose your scroll position.
- **Search box (app.js:35):** it has no close button and no scrim. It closes only on Esc (phones have no Esc) or a second tap on the icon.
findings.proposal:
- **On open:** open() calls history.pushState({ov:1}, "").
- **On back:** a popstate handler calls closeAll().
- **On «سكّر»:** if history.state.ov is set, call history.back().
- **Search:** rebuild it as a .sheet (the same component) with «سكّر» and the scrim.
- Do this before 353 (PWA), because iOS standalone mode has no browser back button.
findings.verified:
Source: ~/workspace/saas/football/site/src/shell.js lines 17-18. open() and closeAll() only toggle `hidden`, the scrim and body.locked. They never call pushState, and there is no popstate listener anywhere in src/*.js or redesign/src/*.js. The only history calls are replaceState: shell.js:43 (the panel writes #anchor), app.js:51 (tabs) and compare.js:38. replaceState replaces the current history entry instead of adding one, so Back goes to the previous page.

Live site: I curled the home page, which loads app, shell, share, v3, render and keyart .235c403a26.js. Each file has 0 matches for pushState|popstate. The source is not stale.

Search: app.js:34-35 builds #srchbox as a .ctrybox div with only an input and results. It has no close button and no scrim. It closes on a second tap of #srch (the top-bar icon, confirmed live in .acts) or on Esc (app.js:45). Tapping outside the box does nothing.

So the claim holds: opening a sheet, the reader panel or search and then pressing Android Back leaves the page.
findings.corrected:
Confirmed, with small corrections. The line numbers are shell.js:17-18, not 14-17. The reader panel does write a #anchor, but with replaceState, so it adds no history entry and Back still leaves the page.

The proposal is sound, with two points to add:
(a) The anchor deep link (shell.js:43, deep() at :50) should use pushState on open. Then Back goes to the same URL without the hash, and popstate calls closeAll().
(b) Search can also close on a tap outside the box.

Guard against double-closing: when «سكّر» calls history.back(), the popstate handler must not run closeAll() again, or the opener focus is restored twice.

findings.title: The tab bar doesn't highlight its own destinations
findings.evidence:
- **Checked with curl:** aria-current appears only on /, /competitions/, /c/*, /m/*, /today/, /t/5789/ and /uae/.
- **No highlight on:** /national/, every /national/xx/, /week/, /arabs/, clubs (/t/102122/), players, coaches, /legends/ and all المزيد pages.
- **Why:** build.cjs:568 (/week/) passes no nav, build_arabs.cjs never sets nav, and team pages get nav "" unless the team is 5789.
findings.proposal:
- In page() (build.cjs:57), derive nk from the path:
  - /national, /arabs, /nations-h2h, /worldcup-arabs → nat
  - /week → week
  - /c, /t (clubs), /p, /coach, /r, /h2h → comps
  - /m → home
- **المزيد pages:** mark the المزيد button itself (aria-current plus the dune underline).
findings.verified:
I checked the live site with curl, looking at the tabbar's aria-current on each page:
- Highlighted correctly: / (اليوم), /competitions/ (البطولات), /uae/ and /t/5789/ (المنتخبات).
- No aria-current at all, although the tabbar renders (status 200, one tabbar each): /national/, /national/sa/, /week/, /arabs/, /t/102122/ and /legends/.

The code explains it:
- build.cjs:58 sets nk from o.nav. A numeric value becomes comps and "uae" becomes nat. With no nav, nothing is highlighted.
- build.cjs:595 (/week/) passes no nav, even though /week/ is one of the four tabs.
- build.cjs:448 (team pages) passes nav:"" for every team except 5789.
- build.cjs:475 (/p/), :605 (/r/), :620 (/coach/) and :342 (/h2h/) pass no nav.
- build_arabs.cjs:22 put() never sets nav, so /arabs/ and every /national/xx/ page get none.
- The only styling is redesign/src/next.css:36/41, which targets [aria-current]. There is no JavaScript fallback that sets it on the client.

The auditor's line numbers are slightly off (/week/ is at build.cjs:595, not 568; page() is at 57–58). The substance holds.
findings.corrected:
The claim is confirmed with small corrections. The /week/ call is at build.cjs:595, not 568, and nk is derived at build.cjs:58.

**Tabs that never highlight on their own pages:**
- الأسبوع is not highlighted on /week/.
- المنتخبات is not highlighted on /national/, any /national/xx/ page or /arabs/. It is highlighted only on /uae/ and /t/5789/.

**Pages with no active tab:** club pages, players, coaches, referees, /h2h/ and /legends/.

The fix proposed in page() stands: work out nk from o.path whenever o.nav is missing.

findings.title: /today/ freezes live scores, and a home rail links to a page that doesn't match its header
findings.evidence:
- **No polling:** run() covers only home, comp, match, team, tv and studio (app.js:351), so /today/ never updates.
- **Frozen score:** at 21:57 UAE, /today/ showed «اليمن 61' 0-0 مباشر» while /v1/live.json had 0-1. The file's last-modified was 17:28 UTC.
- **Mismatched header:** the «مباريات العرب» rail's link says «مباريات بكرة» and goes to /tomorrow/.
- **Also in المزيد:** both /today/ and /tomorrow/ are listed there.
findings.proposal:
- **Rail header links:** go to /?seg=arab#matches or /?d=1#matches, the home list with that segment or day already set.
- **/today/ and /tomorrow/:** add daypage to run(), reusing home's day poll. They stay SEO pages but go live.
- **المزيد:** drop both links.
findings.verified: 1) Code: in ~/workspace/saas/football/site/src/app.js line 351, run() only maps home, comp, match, team, tv and studio. The live /today/ page has <body data-page="daypage">, so no poll starts there. The other live.json pollers in app.js (goal toast at line 286, team ticker at 302, car mode at 308) only cover favourite teams and never redraw the day list. 2) Live site at 18:36 UTC: /today/ had last-modified 17:58:20 GMT, so the static rebuild does run, but about every 40+ minutes. At the same moment its HTML still showed match 6052084 at 86', while /v1/live.json had it finished 0-1. /v1/live.json also had 6052085 (Bahrain v UAE) live at 35' 0-1 and 6150378 live at 33'. So the frozen scores are confirmed. 3) Home HTML: rail id="r-arab" has the header «مباريات العرب» and its more-link says «مباريات بكرة», pointing to /tomorrow/. So the header and link don't match (confirmed). The r-today rail links to /today/ «مباريات اليوم», which is fine. 4) Home nav: the link list has both /today/ «مباريات اليوم» and /tomorrow/ «مباريات بكرة» (confirmed).
findings.corrected: The claim is basically true, with one detail to fix. /today/ is not "never updated". The server rebuilds it every 40+ minutes (last-modified 17:58 UTC when checked at 18:36 UTC). But the page does no live polling in the browser, because data-page="daypage" is missing from run() at app.js:351. So a live match shows a minute and score that can be 40+ minutes old. For example, 6052084 still showed 86' after live.json had it finished 0-1. The home rail «مباريات العرب» (r-arab) has a more-link «مباريات بكرة» that goes to /tomorrow/. Both /today/ and /tomorrow/ are in the home nav list. The fix stands: add daypage to run(), reusing home's day plus live.json merge (line 61/191), and point the r-arab link at an Arab-segment view of the home list.

findings.title: The «ملخص أسبوعك» tab talks to every visitor as that club's fan
findings.evidence:
- **What it says:** the 5th tab on /t/102122/ reads «فريقك الوحدة ما لعب…» and «هالمواجهة بتلعبونها».
- **Who sees it:** every visitor, on every club page.
- **Side effect:** it also takes tab width at 390px.
findings.proposal:
- **Club pages:** remove the tab.
- **Where it goes:** show the digest inside فريقي, or render it client-side only when the club is in tifo.favs.
findings.verified: Code: ~/workspace/saas/football/site/build.cjs:432 sets `wkd = APPROVED.digest ? S.aiDigest(AIDG[id]) : ""`, and build.cjs:436/444 add the «ملخص أسبوعك» tab and pane whenever a digest file exists. Nothing in src/*.js checks tifo.favs or "my team" before showing the pane. It is static HTML served to everyone. Live: `curl https://tifo.elyoxe.com/t/102122/` returns the pane hidden with data-pane="week". Its text is «يديد نادي الوحدة هالأسبوع · فريقك الوحدة ما لعب أي مباراة هالأسبوع … هالمواجهة بتلعبونها تاريخ 1 أكتوبر 2026». So every visitor is addressed as a Al Wahda fan, and the next opponent isn't even named. Coverage: cache/ai/digest has only 14 files, which are the UAE Pro League clubs. On the live site, /t/8540/, /t/5789/ (UAE national team) and /t/8 have no such tab. The screenshot next_team_390_s3c.png is the UAE national page, which has 4 tabs and no digest tab. That means the claim "on every club page" is overstated. The 390px tab-width side effect is not shown in any screenshot I have (no screenshot of a UAE-club team page with 5 tabs), so it is unverified.
findings.corrected: Mostly true, but the scope is narrower. The «ملخص أسبوعك» tab appears only on the 14 UAE Pro League club pages that have a file in cache/ai/digest (for example /t/102122/). It does not appear on every club page or on national-team pages. On those 14 pages the text is fixed at build time and shown to every visitor. It speaks as the club's fan («فريقك الوحدة…», «بتلعبونها») and leaves out the opponent's name. The tab-width cost at 390px is not proven. Fix: remove the tab from the prerendered /t/ pages (build.cjs:436 and :444). Instead, show the digest client-side only when the club id is in tifo.favs, or show it in the فريقي rail. For everyone else, rewrite it in the third person («الوحدة ما لعب…، مباراته الياية ضد X») if it stays.

findings.title: Visitor country is ignored almost everywhere, so the site stays UAE-first for every Arab visitor
findings.evidence:
- **Where country is used:** country() only sets the time zone and re-sorts list:day (app.js:17-19, render.js:102).
- **Hero:** heroPick hardcodes the UAE team (id 5789, +120) and UAE_COMPS (+60) with no country input (v3.js:92-99).
- **Countdown:** #uaecd always loads team/5789.json (app.js:176-177), so every visitor sees the «البحرين ضد الإمارات» countdown.
- **المزيد «اختصارات»:** fixed to دوري أدنوك, /uae/ and كأس الخليج (build.cjs:65).
- **Home competitions grid:** fixed order; Botola is 18th of 18.
- **/competitions/:** UAE comes first and the Premier League sits at about 5300px of 6384px (next_comps_390_full_prod2.png).
- **/week/:** its copy says «مباريات الإمارات أول».
findings.proposal:
- Add one R.me() = {country, league slug, national-team id}, taken from R.COUNTRIES.
- **Hero:** heroPick adds +120 for the visitor's national team and +60 for their league, and drops the hardcoded 5789.
- **Countdown:** #uaecd counts down to the visitor's national team.
- **«اختصارات»:** built client-side as «دوري بلدك · منتخب بلدك · البطولة الشغالة».
- **Competition lists:** the home grid and the /competitions/ groups are reordered with the visitor's country first.
- **/week/:** ranked by the visitor's country.

findings.title: Nav: swap «الأسبوع» (a static UAE-first list) for «فريقي»
findings.evidence:
- **What /week/ is:** 12 prerendered matches: 2 UAE national, 7 UAE League Cup and 3 Botola. No Saudi, Egyptian or Champions League matches.
- **Redundant:** /week/ is already in المزيد and the footer, and the day switcher already reaches the coming days.
- **«فريقك» is buried:** it is home slot 5, at about y 1470 of 3437 (next_home_390_full_feat.png).
- **Roadmap item 5** promised «الصفحة تفتح عليه».
- **Competitors:** FotMob, SofaScore, 365Scores and OneFootball all put Following in the bottom bar.
findings.proposal:
- **Nav:** اليوم · فريقي · البطولات · المنتخبات · المزيد.
- **/mine/ (client page):** one card per favourite club, with its live pulse, last and next match, and table position linked to the table.
- **Empty state:** the 403 crest grid of clubs from the visitor's country.
- **/week/:** moves to المزيد and to the end of the day switcher as a «الأسبوع» cell.

findings.title: Club and player pages have no route to their league or table
findings.evidence:
- **Club page /t/102122/:** the only /c/ links are the fixed المزيد shortcuts.
- **Table position:** it appears only as prose in the 5th tab («الوحدة الحين في المركز 6»).
- **Hero (next_team_390_feat.png):** shows name, coach, stadium and next match, but no league.
- **Taps from club to its table:** البطولات → league → find the row. That is 3 or more taps plus a scroll.
- **Player page /p/15403/:** the crumb shows only the club, with no league, national team or next match (next_player_390_full_s3c.png).
findings.proposal:
- **Team hero kicker:** «دوري أدنوك · المركز 6», linking to /c/<slug>/?hl=<id>#table with the club's row in dune.
- **«الياية» tab:** opens with a 5-row mini table (the club plus 2 rows either side).
- **Player kicker:** «النادي · الدوري · المنتخب», plus a «مباراته الياية» line.

findings.title: One national team has three URLs, and the links between them go one way
findings.evidence:
- **UAE duplicates:** /uae/ and /t/5789/ are identical and each is its own canonical (build.cjs:430 rewrites only the /uae/ copy).
- **Third page:** /national/ae/ carries different content: ranking, last 10 and history.
- **Links go one way:** /t/5789/ has 0 links to /national/ae/.
- **Entry points disagree:** match heroes link to /t/5901/, while المنتخبات leads to /national/bh/.
- **Taps from home to a national team's fixtures:** المنتخبات → row → «المباريات والنتايج» = 3.
findings.proposal:
- **One page per national team** at /national/<iso>/, with tabs الياية · النتايج · اللاعبين · بالأرقام · التاريخ. Today's /national/xx/ content becomes the التاريخ tab.
- **Redirects:** /t/<natId>/ and /uae/ return a 301 to /national/<iso>/.
- **Links:** match heroes and search point there.

findings.title: About 16 pan-Arab pages are orphaned, while المزيد gives space to UAE-only pages
findings.evidence:
- **/arabs/ and its pages** (guide, transfers, derbies, golden-boot, poty, explore, calendars, coefficients, clashes, streaks, year, break, nations-h2h, worldcup-arabs, match-of-week, arabs/week) are absent from the nav, المزيد (build.cjs:65-68) and the footer (build.cjs:84).
- **The only home link:** a small «عالم العرب» inside the «أقوى الأندية العربية» panel, 3 taps deep.
- **Wrong «وين تنقل»:** it points to /watch/ (UAE channels only), while /guide/ (a TV guide per Arab country) is orphaned.
- **UAE-only content under generic labels:** 7 of the 22 المزيد links.
findings.proposal:
- **المنتخبات landing:** gets the /arabs/ tiles as a shelf, becoming «المنتخبات والعرب».
- **New المزيد group «العرب»:** المحترفين برا · الانتقالات · الحذاء الذهبي · الديربيات · أرشيف النتايج.
- **«وين تنقل»:** points to /guide/, which is country-aware.
- **UAE pages:** grouped under «كورة الإمارات».
- **Footer:** the 396 footer columns should mirror these groups.

findings.title: Search: identical names without context, a blank empty state, and big gaps in the index
findings.evidence:
- **Identical names** in search.b7cd0e7729.json (4957 items): 3× النصر, 3× الأهلي, and 2× each of الوحدة, الشباب, القادسية and العربي.
- **No context:** each row shows only «نادي» (app.js:40).
- **Missing Arabic names:** 71 teams.

lenses.summary:
I audited the match page for tonight's live match (/m/6052085/, Bahrain v UAE) and two finished ones (/m/1000020522/, /m/1000020526/). I used the screenshots, curl of the pages and the API, the code, and the v3 worktree diff; nothing was edited.

The page's building blocks are good: key-art hero, «ليش هالنتيجة؟», win probability, «لو خلصت الحين», goal moment, and per-country channels. The problems are trust and live feel.
- **Kickoff lag:** at kickoff the match file said "scheduled" for at least 100 seconds while live.json already showed minute 1–2.
- **Live timeline order:** during a live match the newest event sits at the bottom of a long list.
- **Stats contradict events:** the stats tab says 0–0 yellow cards while the event list shows 5, and prints a dozen false zeros.
- **Names on the pitch:** they cut Arabic compound names («الله حمد», «الدين زهير»).
- **Invisible match line:** the goal marker and the played bar are invisible because of a build colour remap. Item 392 moves this bug into «خط المباراة».
- **Wrong or empty content:** the AI preview says Bahrain is at home, but the match is in Jeddah. The H2H list shows a future match as «انتهت», and the «أوائل» tile calls it a first meeting when there are 20 earlier ones. The analysis tab is filled with filler and journalist tools, and the share sheet has 13 rows, 4 of them overlapping big-screen modes.
- **Easy wins:** a «شو على المحك» card before group games (tonight a UAE win would give 6 points in Group B), naming the player of the match, the exact highlight video with its thumbnail, and scorers on the share images.

Flags on the design agent's items:
- **392:** carry a `.tl` colour override and use the API's `momentum`. Nothing reads it today.
- **389:** the sub arrows use live green.
- **391:** the duplication goes beyond «الخلاصة» into the analysis tab.
- **393:** the hero's primary button should change with the match state rather than always being share.

Paths: /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/render.js, /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/shell.js, /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/v3.css, /root/workspace/saas/football/site/build.cjs, /root/workspace/saas/football/poller.py, /root/workspace/saas/football/store.py.

findings.title: At kickoff the match page lags live.json by 100+ seconds (scheduled file is cached 300s + 60s stale)
findings.evidence: 22:02:10–22:03:37 UAE: /v1/live.json said 6052085 live, minute 1→2. /v1/match/6052085.json still said scheduled: cache-control max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=60, age 308, last-modified 17:16Z. poller.py:317 gives 'warm' to any scheduled match, and app.js:151 polls only the match JSON.
findings.proposal: poller.py:317: use cache='hot' when a scheduled match is within the prematch window (ko-75min..ko+15). app.js match(): on each 20s poll also read live.json (10s TTL), overlay status, minute and score onto MD before rendering, and refetch the full JSON only when the score or status changed.
findings.verified: Code: in ~/workspace/saas/football/poller.py:317 (build/lambda/poller.py:314 is the same), a match file gets cache="hot" only when the match is live, "static" when finished, and "warm" otherwise. That includes the prematch fetches that live_pass (poller.py:396-397) runs every 2 minutes from ko-75min up to ko. store.py:27 maps "warm" to "public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=60". store.py put_json skips the write when the content is unchanged, which explains the old last-modified of 17:16Z. Nothing in the Python code invalidates CloudFront (grepped for "invalidat": no hits). Client: app.js:11 fetches with cache:"no-cache", which only revalidates the browser cache. CloudFront still serves its own edge copy until max-age plus SWR run out. app.js:145-153 match() polls only match/ID.json, every 20s while live or within 90 minutes of kickoff. It never reads live.json. Live check at 22:34 UAE: live.json has max-age=10. match/6052085.json has now switched to max-age=20 (hot) and reports status live, minute 33, score 0-1. So the problem only lasts from the scheduled-to-live flip until the edge copy expires. Once a hot copy is cached, the page tracks the match fine.
findings.corrected: Confirmed, and the worst case is bigger than the claim says. The last prematch write of match/{id}.json is cached at the CloudFront edge with max-age=300 and stale-while-revalidate=60, and nothing invalidates it on kickoff. A user who opens the match page when it starts can see «scheduled» for up to about 360s (the auditor measured 100+s), even though live.json already shows minute 1-2. After that the file is hot (20s) and the page keeps up. Minimal fix: at poller.py:317, use cache="hot" for a scheduled match inside the prematch window (ko-75min to ko+15min). That alone brings the worst-case lag down to about 40s. The app.js live.json overlay is an optional extra: it lowers the lag to about 20s and shows the kickoff flip at once.

findings.title: Stats tab contradicts the events and prints fake zeros
findings.evidence: 1000020522 stats: «الإنذارات 0 | 0», but the events list has 5 yellows (34', 51', 70', 83', 90+1'). 1000020526 (coverage 'lower'): «الإنذارات 0 0», and «من داخل المنطقة 0 0 / من برا المنطقة 0 0» against 19 total shots, plus 10 more 0|0 rows. 29 flat rows, with no leader emphasis.
findings.proposal: R.stats (render.js:202): count yellow and red cards from md.events. When coverage≠full, drop rows where both sides are 0. Show 6 top rows (possession, xG if any, shots, on target, big chances, corners), then a «كل الأرقام» toggle. Bold the leading side's value in a chalk pill.
findings.verified:
I fetched the live pages /m/1000020522/ and /m/1000020526/ with curl and parsed the stat rows and the event classes. I also read R.stats in ~/workspace/saas/football/site/src/render.js:201-207. R.stats prints every key in STAT_AR that the provider sends, as a flat list. It never checks values against md.events, never drops 0|0 rows, and never emphasises the leading side.

Match 1000020522 has 29 stat rows. «الإنذارات» shows 0|0 and «الطرد» shows 0|0. The same page has 5 yellow-card events (5 x `ico yellow`, with `ev yellow h/a` rows).

Match 1000020526 has 28 stat rows. 15 of them are 0|0: فرص محققة، فرص ضايعة، الإنذارات، القائم والعارضة، من داخل/برا المنطقة، كرات طويلة صحيحة، عرضيات صحيحة، قطع الكورة، إبعاد، التحامات ناجحة/أرضية، كرات هوائية، مراوغات، الطرد. That match has 19|15 shots and also 5 yellow events.

The /v1/matches/{id}.json path returned something that is not JSON, so I could not confirm coverage='lower' from the API.
findings.corrected:
The claim is essentially confirmed. A few details are off:
- 1000020526 renders 28 rows, not 29, and 15 of them are 0|0, which is more than the claim counted. 1000020522 does render 29 rows.
- «الطرد 0|0» is also wrong on both pages if any red event exists. The card fix should count yellows and reds from md.events.
- I did not confirm coverage='lower' from the API. So the zero-row filter should be: drop any row where both sides are 0, except cards (always taken from events) and possession.
- Also drop the in-box/out-of-box shot rows when both are 0 while total shots is above 0.

The proposal otherwise stands: show about 6 key rows, put the rest behind a «كل الأرقام» toggle, and emphasise the leading side's value.

findings.title: Pitch names cut Arabic compound names: «الله حمد», «الدين زهير», «الله الخلاصي»
findings.evidence: surname() at render.js:183 drops the first word after arNames() has made the names Arabic. Seen in next_match_390_lineups_final («الدين زهير», «الله حمد») and next_live_390_lineups_final («الله الخلاصي», on tonight's UAE/Bahrain pitch).
findings.proposal: For Arabic names: keep the full name if it has 2 words or fewer; otherwise glue prefixes to the next word (عبد، أبو، بن، ابن، and علاء/نور/سيف/عز/صلاح/شمس + الدين) before taking the tail. Better: add short_ar to names/players_ar.json and prefer it.
findings.verified:
Confirmed. Three checks agree:
1. Code: src/render.js:183 is `surname(n){ var p=n.split(/\s+/); return p.length>1 ? p.slice(1).join(" ") : p[0]; }`. It drops the first word of the name. pitchSide (render.js:190) calls it on names that R.arNames (src/v3.js:20, wrapped around R.lineups at v3.js:32) has already turned into Arabic. So «علاء الدين زهير» comes out as «الدين زهير» and «عبد الله حمد» as «الله حمد».
2. Screenshots: next_match_390_lineups_final.png shows «الله حمد» (12) and «الدين زهير» (5), while the list below the pitch shows the full «علاء الدين زهير». next_live_390_lineups_final.png shows «الدين زهير» (UAE 5) and «الله الخلاصى» (Bahrain 23).
3. Live site: curl of /m/6052085/ right now returns pitch labels «الله الخلاصي» and «الدين زهير». It also returns «عبد الجبار حسن», which shows the rule keeps leftover words inconsistently.
findings.corrected: The claim is right; I'd change one part of the proposal. Keeping the full name whenever it has 2 words or fewer would make pitch labels long on a 390px phone (e.g. «فاكوندو إنسفران»). Glue the compound first (عبد/أبو/بن/ابن plus the next word, and any word followed by الدين or الله), then show only the last unit. That gives «زهير», «حمد» and «الخلاصي». A single-word or one-unit name stays whole. Longer term, prefer short_ar from names/players_ar.json when it exists. The fix goes in surname() at render.js:183.

findings.title: Goal markers and the played bar on the match line are invisible (build remap); item 392 inherits the bug
findings.evidence: build.cjs:150 sw('chalk','surf') turns '.tl .ev.goal' and '.tl .played' into var(--surf) #123A31 on night (confirmed in the live tifo.6b99163974.css). The pixel at the 10' goal in next_match_1440_feat is rgb(18,58,49), while the yellow cards are bright. The v3 diff moves the timeline to التحليل «خط المباراة» with no .tl override. No code in either tree reads the API's per-minute `momentum` (present e.g. /v1/match/5795459.json) or the match `shotmap`.
findings.proposal: v3.css: '.tl .ev.goal{background:var(--ink)} .tl .played{background:var(--ink)}'. Draw goals as a chalk circle, larger than the card ticks. For 392, draw the curve from md.momentum when present, and add the match shotmap by reusing S.shotmap (stats.js:211) for xG-coverage matches.
findings.verified: 1) build.cjs:150: `sw("chalk","surf")` rewrites any `background:...var(--chalk)` to var(--surf). src/tifo.css:149 `.tl .played{...background:var(--chalk)}` and :153 `.tl .ev.goal{background:var(--chalk)}` both match. 2) The live CSS (assets/tifo.235c403a26.css, taken from /m/6052085/) really has `.tl .played{...background:var(--surf)}` and `.tl .ev.goal{background:var(--surf)}`, with --surf:#123A31 on the v3 :root. The only later `.tl` rule is `.mhero .tl .axis{background:#F6F7F233}` (v3.css:83), so there is no override for goals or the played bar. 3) In next_match_1440_feat.png the yellow cards are bright squares, but the 10' goal at the right end of the line (near x≈1209, y≈422) is an almost invisible dark-green square, and no played bar can be seen. This is a real bug in the live match hero. 4) The v3 worktree (~/workspace/saas/football-v3/site) still has the same tifo.css:149/153 and applies the same remap, and its v3.css/next.css have no `.tl .ev.goal` or `.tl .played` override. 5) /v1/match/5795459.json does contain `momentum` (a per-minute list of {minute,value}) and `shotmap`. Grepping both trees for `momentum` in src/, redesign/src and build.cjs finds no consumer. 6) The proposed fix `var(--ink)` is safe: v3 :root sets --ink:#F6F7F2 (chalk). var(--chalk) would be clearer.
findings.corrected: The claim is mostly true; one detail is overstated. The build remap (build.cjs:150 sw chalk→surf) makes `.tl .ev.goal` and `.tl .played` #123A31 on the night ground in the live CSS and in the v3 branch. As a result, goals and the played bar on the match line are invisible, while cards are visible (next_match_1440_feat). The API's per-minute `momentum` is not read anywhere. The overstated part: the match `shotmap` is read, but only in src/shell.js:214, which filters `md.shotmap` down to one player's sheet. The match-level shot map is never drawn on the match page; only the player page uses S.shotmap (build.cjs:473). Fix: in v3.css add `.tl .ev.goal,.tl .played{background:var(--chalk)}`, and make the goal a larger chalk circle (for example `border-radius:50%;inline-size:.9rem;block-size:.9rem`). Or exempt `.tl` from the sw() remap. For 392, draw the curve from md.momentum and reuse S.shotmap on md.shotmap for matches that have xG coverage.

findings.title: H2H shows a future match as «انتهت», rows have no dates, and «أوائل» claims a first meeting
findings.evidence: 1000020526 H2H first row links /m/1000021967/ (kickoff 2026-10-18, score null) with the chip «انتهت», because render.js:212 forces m.status||'finished'. Rows call R.matchRow(m,{}) with no date or year. The same page's «أوائل» tile says «أول مواجهة بين الفريقين في بياناتنا»; H2H summary: 3/6/11 (20 earlier meetings).
findings.proposal: R.h2h: skip matches with no score, or list them under «الياية». Use R.matchRow(m,{date:true}) and add the year and competition. Put «كل مواجهاتهم» under the list. Emit firsts.first_meeting only when h2h.matches is empty, or phrase it as «أول مرة في كأس الرابطة».
findings.verified:
I checked the live page https://tifo.elyoxe.com/m/1000020526/ with curl and confirmed all three parts of the claim.
1. The first H2H row links /m/1000021967/, Ajman v Sharjah, with the chip «انتهت» (chip off). The live page for that match gives startDate 2026-10-18T19:45+04:00, so the match hasn't been played. Note: /v1/matches/1000021967.json returns 404, so I took the date from the page's structured data, not from the API.
2. The cause is src/render.js:212, which sets `m.status = m.status || "finished"` and then calls `R.matchRow(m, {})`. That call passes no date option, and the rendered rows show no date, year or competition.
3. The H2H summary on the same page reads 3 / 6 / 11 (Ajman wins / draws / Sharjah wins), which is 20 earlier meetings. The page still shows «أول مواجهة بين الفريقين في بياناتنا (من موسم 2010/11)», twice. That text comes from src/stats.js:548, which renders the kind first_meeting. The flag itself is set in compute/insights.py:404-406 when `history_rows` has no earlier meeting between the two teams, so that history source misses the meetings the h2h summary counts.
findings.corrected: The claim is confirmed as stated. A more precise root cause for the «أوائل» part: compute/insights.py:404-406 decides first_meeting from `history_rows`, and that data does not contain the 20 meetings that md.h2h counts. The fix belongs there: skip first_meeting whenever md.h2h.summary has any meetings. The stats.js text is only where it gets displayed.

findings.title: Analysis tab is padded with filler tiles and journalist tools (extends 391)
findings.evidence: 1000020522: the only tiles are «الخطط والتبديلات» («5 تبديلات، أولها الدقيقة 46»), «أوائل» (Latin «Vladimir Prijović») and «إعادة المباراة» (next_match_390_scrolled_final). 6052085 before kickoff: «البحرين خطة 4-1-4-1، 0 تبديلات», taken from the last lineup, while the official API lineup is 4-2-3-1. «ورقة الصحفي» comes with «وضع المعلّق · اطبعها». 1000020526 has 5 AI texts (why, الخلاصة, الخلاصة بالذكاء الاصطناعي, ثريد إكس, التعليق).
findings.proposal: Delete the «الخطط والتبديلات» tile, since the formation is on the pitch. Move «ورقة الصحفي» and «ثريد إكس» to /m/<id>/kit/. For finished matches keep one AI text in the first tab (why) and drop «الخلاصة بالذكاء الاصطناعي». Show «أوائل» only when it is a real milestone. Keep 4 tiles or fewer.
findings.verified:
I fetched /m/1000020522/, /m/6052085/ and /m/1000020526/ with curl, pulled the headings from each, and compared them with build.cjs:494-506 and src/stats.js:252-267. I also checked /v1/match/6052085.json.

What holds up. On 522 the tiles in «التحليل كله» are «الخطط والتبديلات» («خطة 4-1-4-1، 5 تبديلات، أولها الدقيقة 46»), «أوائل» («أول مشاركة لـ Vladimir Prijović هالموسم», with the name in Latin) and «إعادة المباراة». On 526 the same three tiles come after «التعليق», «الخلاصة بالذكاء الاصطناعي» and «ثريد إكس».

What is wrong or out of date:
(1) 6052085 now shows «خطة 4-4-2، 0 تبديلات». That matches the API: lineups.type is "standard", home (Bahrain) plays 4-4-2 and away (UAE) plays 4-2-3-1. The 4-1-4-1 mismatch was pre-kickoff data from the last lineup and it has been fixed. The «0 تبديلات» part is still weak.
(2) «ورقة الصحفي» with «وضع المعلّق · اطبعها» is not on any of these pages now. build.cjs:495 renders the press sheet only for scheduled UAE matches, so it is not filler on normal or finished matches.
(3) 526 does not have 5 AI texts, it has 3: التعليق, الخلاصة بالذكاء الاصطناعي and ثريد إكس. The «الخلاصة» box (#catchup) is built from match facts, not AI («عجمان فاز 3 - 2. الأهداف: …»). The «why» item is just a link to /laws/ («ليش ألغى الحكم هدف…»), not AI text.
(4) Removing the duplicate «الخلاصة» is already polish item 387–403, so that part is not new.
findings.corrected:
[remove/medium] On finished matches the analysis tab has two weak tiles and too much AI text. «الخطط والتبديلات» repeats the formation already on the pitch, and on the live 6052085 it says «0 تبديلات» even though SCHEMA.md says the Gulf Cup feed never reports substitutions. «أوائل» shows trivia with a Latin name («أول مشاركة لـ Vladimir Prijović هالموسم»). Finished matches with AI turned on (1000020526) have 3 AI blocks («التعليق», «الخلاصة بالذكاء الاصطناعي», «ثريد إكس») on top of the fact-based «الخلاصة».

Proposal:
- Drop the «الخطط والتبديلات» tile, or hide the substitution count when coverage_events.subs is false.

- Leave the journalist sheet («ورقة الصحفي») alone. It already shows only on scheduled UAE matches.

findings.title: Lineup builder formation grid is broken: 4-3-3 renders as 2/1/2/1/2/2/1
findings.evidence: feat_xi.png: 11 native selects wrap 2 per line, so 4-3-3 shows rows of 2,1,2,1,2,2,1. shell.js:212 outputs .xr rows, and the live CSS has no .xr rule (only .xi). Each select lists the whole squad unsorted.
findings.proposal: CSS: '.xr{display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:.4rem}.xr select{flex:1;min-inline-size:0}'. Group options with optgroup by squad group (حارس/دفاع/وسط/هجوم), and limit the keeper slot to keepers.
findings.verified: feat_xi.png: with 4-3-3 selected, the 11 selects render in rows of 2,1,2,1,2,2,1 (attack 3 → 2+1, midfield 3 → 2+1, defence 4 → 2+2, keeper 1). That symptom is real. The builder markup is at src/shell.js:233, not :212. It wraps each formation line in <div class="xr">. The claim that the live CSS has no .xr rule is FALSE. The live /assets/tifo.235c403a26.css and src/v3.css:421-422 both contain `.xr{display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:.4rem;flex-wrap:wrap}` and `.xr select{max-inline-size:9.5rem;...}`. The actual cause is flex-wrap:wrap. Each select is about 152px wide with a 0.4rem gap, and the box is about 320px inside at 390px width, so only 2 fit per line. The option list comes from shell.js:231: sq is built by walking t.squad group by group (coach excluded). So the list is in squad-group order, not random, but it has no optgroup labels and the keeper slot is not filtered.
findings.corrected: [broken/low] On phones the lineup builder breaks the formation lines. The .xr rule does exist (src/v3.css:421), but it combines flex-wrap:wrap with a select max-inline-size of 9.5rem. At 390px only 2 selects fit per line, so 4-3-3 shows as 2/1/2/1/2/2/1 (feat_xi.png). Fix in src/v3.css:421-422: drop flex-wrap and use `.xr select{flex:1 1 0;min-inline-size:0;max-inline-size:9.5rem}` so a line of 3 or 4 always stays on one row. Separately, in shell.js:233, group the options with <optgroup> by g.group (حارس/دفاع/وسط/هجوم), since sq already carries g, and limit the keeper slot (row 0) to goalkeepers.

findings.title: Live events list runs oldest→newest, so the newest event is at the bottom
findings.evidence: R.events (render.js:158) is always ascending. On 1000020522 the list runs about 1,900px on 390 (next_match_390_full_feat), so a live goal appears off-screen. The AI commentary on the same page says «والأحدث فوق». set() (app.js:15) replaces the whole pane every 20s, with no marker on the new row.
findings.proposal: While R.isLive(md): render newest first, with period dividers reversed too. Give rows whose first_seen (already stamped in poller.py:303) is under 90s old a 2s chalk flash. Diff by event_id instead of replacing innerHTML. Optionally show the matching Emirati commentary line (AICM) under goal and red-card rows only, and drop the separate «التعليق» tile.

Build them from standings and remaining fixtures by reusing 370's R.liveTable with hypothetical scores. Confirm the advancement format from comp data before writing «تتأهل».
